title: Data file types nrtype 1, 3 and 4
purpose: Exercises the readers of the three non-GUDRUN data formats of the `epsr` engine of EPSR [@soper1996,@soper2005] ("read in data to be fitted" in `runepsr17`): `nrtype 1` two-column Q S(Q), `nrtype 3` GENIE histogram listing and `nrtype 4` GENIE point listing [@epsrmanual]. Users with data from other reduction programs depend on these paths.
fortran: `epsr_standalone_rev3.f`: `runepsr17` (data reading: list-directed `nrtype 1`, `(i7,3g14.7)` with header records for `nrtype 3/4`, histogram-to-centre Q conversion, ignored last point)
rust: `datafile.rs`: `read_data_points` (fixed-format `(i7,3g14.7)` read with BLANK=NULL/PAD semantics, iostat chain of the header reads)
system: The EPSR-test system: a liquid mixture of 200 dimethyl sulphoxide (DMSO, (CH3)2SO) and 400 water molecules (DMSO mole fraction 1/3; 3200 atoms) at 300 K in a cubic box of side 33.12 Å (atomic number density 0.0881 atoms/Å³). DMSO uses EPSR's Lennard-Jones + Coulomb reference potential with methyl rotational groups; water uses SPC/E Lennard-Jones and charge parameters [@berendsen1987] with EPSR's flexible intramolecular geometry (O-H 0.976 Å). The empirical potential is refined against three neutron diffraction data sets of deuterated DMSO in D2O, in null-scattering H2O/D2O and in H2O (ISIS SANDALS runs SLS03863, SLS03871, SLS03850), the isotope-substitution approach of Soper and Luzar [@soperluzar1992]. Here the three data sets are supplied in three different formats: data 1 (`D6DMSO_D2O.nrt1`) as headerless list-directed `Q S(Q)` (errors set to 0) at bin centres; data 2 (`D6DMSO_HDO.nrt3`) in GENIE format with 4 header lines and histogram bin boundaries, converted to centres by EPSR; data 3 (`D6DMSO_H2O.nrt4`) in GENIE point format with an extra rubbish last point (S = 9.99) which EPSR ignores.
inputs: `scripts/make_data.py` writes the three files from the base `.mint01` files (kept in the folder); `scripts/make_inp.sh` sets `datafile` and `nrtype` in the `.EPSR.inp` via `scripts/setkw.py`.
verification: All three files give 594 points (log `Read 594 points from file ...`), the same as the original `.mint01` data; the identical outputs show that the record positioning of the Fortran was reproduced exactly.
notes: Fortran quirks reproduced: for `nrtype 1` the first record is read and then `backspace`d, so the first line is data and the last point kept; for `nrtype 3/4` record 1 plus 4 records are read before backspacing, so record 5 is the first data line, and the last point is dropped.
